messages:
sam: paging: alert from infra - sustained error-rate spike + increased latency on /v1/generate. errors look like bad token decoding and occasional cross-request content leakage. tagging @eng-oncall.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #1769504321 - KV cache staleness / reuse correctness (severity: P1). page: @eng-oncall.
maria: seeing a big jump in cache evictions and sudden growth in KV store size on gpu-pool-3, also CPU+network bandwidth spike. can reproduce locally: responses include tokens from previous unrelated requests.
jordan: confirmed in traces — several requests returned embeddings with seq_offset mismatches; KV entries have seq_offset values that don't line up with request ids. example log below:
```
2026-03-15T10:14:02Z [kv-cache] key=ctx-7f3a val_seq=145 expected_seq=0 origin=req-8b9f
2026-03-15T10:14:02Z [serve] request=req-8b9f batch=12 model=gpt-open-quantized returned_from_cache=true
2026-03-15T10:14:02Z [serve] warn: cache value seq_offset != request.seq -> possible reuse across sessions
```
lee: immediate impact: hosted users on region-us-west-2 see ~2.7% incorrect-output rate (noise + wrong completions). Some large customers running multitenant workloads may have had PII cross-taint risk. we've started a customer notification draft.
anya: attempted quick mitigation: toggled feature-flag `enable_kv_reuse` -> false on canary; pushed policy to route all production traffic for model `gpt-open-quantized` to no-cache variant.
ops-bot: Runbook step executed: scaled up dedicated fallback pool by +20% capacity; entered maintenance mode for gpu-pool-3.
maria: small reproduction notes: when continuous batching is enabled with batch_size > 8 and prefix_caching on, the cache key generation logic sometimes omits request sequence salt. suspect race in key rotation when batches merge.
jordan: logs show two patterns: (1) cache.insert with missing request_ns tag; (2) cache.get returning entry for different request_id but matching short hash. This explains stale keys/values and cross-request leakage.
sam: we need a hotfix. Proposal: immediate patch to runtime to include request_nonce in cache key derivation and force full KV invalidation for last 10m in affected hosts. Also change batching config: max_batch_size=8 and disable batch-merging heuristic.
lee: i'll open a hotfix PR and cut a canary image. PR refs: `github.com/redwood/serve@hotfix/kv-key-nonce`
anja: (typo fix) -> anya: bringing @maria and @jordan onto rollback plan.
incident-bot: Hotfix steps: patch deployed to canary hosts (2/6) at 10:25 UTC; monitoring for incorrect-output-rate, cache_size, and latency.
maria: canary metrics look good so far: incorrect-output-rate for canary dropped to 0.1% after key-change, latency unchanged. However cache size temporarily spiked after invalidation as client prefixes were re-added.
jordan: to avoid cache blowup, we should throttle prefix re-population. Suggest a backoff on prefix writes: if invalidation occurred, reject new writes for 30s per cache shard.
lee: deployed config change to throttle writes and adjusted `prefix_repopulation_backoff=30s`.
ops-bot: Metric alerts suppressed for canary hosts during repopulation window.
sam: timelines for full rollout? If canary remains stable for 20m, roll to rest of pool in staged waves with feature flag on rollback path.
anya: starting staged rollout at 10:48 UTC. wave 1 -> 10 hosts, wave 2 -> 30 hosts at 11:00, wave 3 -> remaining.
(10:55) maria: during rollout a perf cliff observed in wave 2: tail latency for short requests spiked x4 for a subset of pods. root cause: added nonce computation increased CPU in hot path; combined with repopulation it caused GC pressure.
jordan: mitigation for perf cliff: revert nonce compute to optimized inline path (low-overhead), enable lightweight async nonce precompute to avoid blocking token emission. also lowered `max_concurrent_prefill` from 64 -> 16.
lee: applied optimized nonce code and reduced prefill concurrency; tail latency recovered within ~3 minutes.
sam: customer impact summary draft: "Some customers experienced incorrect responses and, in rare cases, content from other requests. No confirmed data exfiltration beyond ephemeral tokens. We are proactively contacting top 10 affected customers and offering rollbacks/credits. Full postmortem will follow."
anya: prepared notification to security & compliance for potential cross-tenant exposure.
maria: follow-up action items (short):
- short-term: run full KV audit to list keys with mismatched seq_offsets (maria, jordan)
- mid-term: add strong unit tests for key derivation and batching boundary conditions (jordan)
- infra: enable rate-limited prefix writes and monitoring for cache growth per-shard (lee)
- customer: notify affected and offer mitigation plan (sam, anya)
jordan: preliminary root cause hypothesis: a race in continuous batching where merged batches reused a base cache key that was computed without request_nonce when batch boundaries cross worker boundaries. The reuse logic assumed idempotent prefix keys but missed sequence-dependent offsets.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity remains P1. assigned owners: maria (root cause), lee (infra), jordan (runtime), sam (customer comms).
sam: handoff to next on-call at 12:00 UTC — @eng-oncall take over monitoring and coordinate postmortem doc creation.
eng-oncall: acknowledged. will keep the channel open and prepare timeline + metrics dashboard link: https://console.redwood/ops/incidents/1769504321
lee: uploading hotfix PR and patches to the incident doc. PR link: https://github.com/redwood/serve/pull/4921
anya: notes for postmortem: include diff of cache key hashing, explain how batch-merging heuristic interacts with key derivation, and list mitigations and timeline.
sam: thanks team — keep updates in thread. next steps: stabilize, finish customer comms, and schedule a follow-up blameless postmortem this week.
eng-oncall: closing pager for night; will re-open if anomalies > 0.5% incorrect-output-rate or signs of cross-tenant leakage.
